        "modality_explanation": "The text states an employee 'must provide notice' when the approximate timing of the need for leave is not foreseeable.",
        "statement": "When the approximate timing of the need for leave is not foreseeable, an employee must provide notice to the employer as soon as practicable under the facts and circumstances of the particular case.",

        "modality": "must",

        "modality_explanation": "The source uses 'generally should be practicable', denoting a recommendation/general expectation.",
        "statement": "It generally should be practicable for the employee to provide notice of leave that is unforeseeable within the time prescribed by the employer's usual and customary notice requirements applicable to such leave (see § 825.303(c)).",
        "kind": "recommendation",
        "modality": "should",
        "scope_text": null,

        "modality_explanation": "The source specifies 'Notice may be given... if the employee is unable to do so personally', conferring permission.",
        "statement": "Notice of unforeseeable leave may be given by the employee's spokesperson (e.g., spouse, adult family member, or other responsible party) if the employee is unable to do so personally.",

        "modality": "may",
        "scope_text": "if the employee is unable to do so personally",

        "choice_quote": null,

        "references": null
      }
    },

      "unit": "F001",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "modality_explanation": "The phrase 'would not be required' explicitly denotes an absence of duty under the stated emergency example.",
        "statement": "For example, if an employee's child has a severe asthma attack and the employee takes the child to the emergency room, the employee would not be required to leave his or her child in order to report the absence while the child is receiving emergency treatment.",
        "kind": "exemption",
        "modality": "not_required",
        "scope_text": "if an employee's child has a severe asthma attack and the employee takes the child to the emergency room, while the child is receiving emergency treatment",
        "scope_quotes": ["F001"],
        "context_quotes": null,
        "modality_quote": "would not be required",
        "choice_text": null,
        "choice_quote": null,
        "alternative_quotes": null,
        "logic_quote": null,
        "references": null
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F001",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "modality_explanation": "The phrase 'would be expected' sets a baseline normative expectation/recommendation under the specified condition.",
        "statement": "If a child's asthma attack required only the use of an inhaler at home followed by a period of rest, the employee would be expected to call the employer promptly after ensuring the child has used the inhaler.",
        "kind": "recommendation",
        "modality": "should",
        "scope_text": "if the child's asthma attack required only the use of an inhaler at home followed by a period of rest",
        "scope_quotes": ["F001"],

        "choice_text": null,
        "choice_quote": null,

        "references": null
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F002",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "modality_explanation": "'An employee shall provide' establishes a mandatory duty.",
        "statement": "An employee shall provide sufficient information for an employer to reasonably determine whether the FMLA may apply to the leave request.",
        "kind": "requirement",
        "modality": "must",
        "scope_text": null,
        "scope_quotes": null,

        "choice_text": null,

        "logic_quote": null,
        "references": null
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F002",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "modality_explanation": "The text states 'such information may include', denoting descriptive illustrative possibilities depending on the situation.",
        "statement": "Depending on the situation, information sufficient to determine if FMLA may apply may include: that a condition renders the employee unable to perform the functions of the job; that the employee is pregnant or has been hospitalized overnight; whether the employee or the employee's family member is under the continuing care of a health care provider; if the leave is due to a qualifying exigency, that a military member is on covered active duty or call to covered active duty status (or has been notified of an impending call or order to covered active duty), that the requested leave is for one of the reasons listed in § 825.126(b), and the anticipated duration of the absence; or if the leave is for a family member, that the condition renders the family member unable to perform daily activities or that the family member is a covered servicemember with a serious injury or illness; and the anticipated duration of the absence, if known.",
        "kind": "statement",
        "modality": "possible",
        "scope_text": "Depending on the situation",
        "scope_quotes": ["F002"],
        "context_quotes": null,
        "modality_quote": "may include",
        "choice_text": null,
        "choice_quote": null,
        "alternative_quotes": null,
        "logic_quote": null,
        "references": ["§ 825.126(b)"]
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F002",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "modality_explanation": "'The employee need not expressly assert' states an explicit absence of duty.",
        "statement": "When an employee seeks leave for the first time for a FMLA-qualifying reason, the employee need not expressly assert rights under the FMLA or even mention the FMLA.",
        "kind": "exemption",
        "modality": "not_required",
        "scope_text": "When an employee seeks leave for the first time for a FMLA-qualifying reason",
        "scope_quotes": ["F002"],
        "context_quotes": null,
        "modality_quote": "need not",

        "choice_quote": null,
        "alternative_quotes": null,

        "modality_explanation": "'The employee must specifically reference' creates an obligation.",
        "statement": "When an employee seeks leave due to a qualifying reason for which the employer has previously provided the employee FMLA-protected leave, the employee must specifically reference either the qualifying reason for leave or the need for FMLA leave.",
        "kind": "requirement",
        "modality": "must",
        "scope_text": "When an employee seeks leave due to a qualifying reason, for which the employer has previously provided the employee FMLA-protected leave",
        "scope_quotes": ["F002"],
        "context_quotes": null,
        "modality_quote": "must",
        "choice_text": "The employee must specifically reference either the qualifying reason for leave or the need for FMLA leave.",

        "logic_quote": null,
        "references": null

        "statement": "Calling in “sick” without providing more information will not be considered sufficient notice to trigger an employer's obligations under the Act.",
        "kind": "statement",
        "modality": "not_stated",
        "scope_text": null,

        "statement": "An employee has an obligation to respond to an employer's questions designed to determine whether an absence is potentially FMLA-qualifying.",
        "kind": "requirement",
        "modality": "must",
        "scope_text": null,

        "statement": "Failure to respond to reasonable employer inquiries regarding the leave request may result in denial of FMLA protection if the employer is unable to determine whether the leave is FMLA-qualifying.",
        "kind": "statement",
        "modality": "possible",
        "scope_text": "if the employer is unable to determine whether the leave is FMLA-qualifying",
        "scope_quotes": ["F002"],

        "statement": "When the need for leave is not foreseeable, an employee must comply with the employer's usual and customary notice and procedural requirements for requesting leave, absent unusual circumstances.",
        "kind": "requirement",
        "modality": "must",
        "scope_text": "When the need for leave is not foreseeable, absent unusual circumstances",

        "statement": "If an employee requires emergency medical treatment, he or she would not be required to follow the call-in procedure until his or her condition is stabilized and he or she has access to, and is able to use, a phone.",

        "statement": "Similarly, in the case of an emergency requiring leave because of a FMLA-qualifying reason, written advance notice pursuant to an employer's internal rules and procedures may not be required when FMLA leave is involved.",
        "kind": "statement",
